results.notes: Each Pivot phase uses two communication rounds, followed by one round for cluster assignment. Independently sampled finite ranks create a vanishing correction. results.theorem: Algorithm 1, Lemma 3.3, and Theorem 3.9; explicit β=λ=1/36 in the proof; LOCAL round implementation derived here
assumptions: Exact closed-neighborhood comparison
Unique vertex IDs
No restriction on LOCAL message size
results.notes: Derivation: one round exchanges closed neighborhoods and determines agreement; one exchanges heavy/light flags; four rounds propagate the maximum ID in each trimmed component (diameter at most four by Lemma 3.3). Six rounds suffice with known neighbor IDs; allow one additional initial ID exchange otherwise. Theorem 3.9 explicitly certifies 1442 for these parameters. We do not use approximately optimized 701 as an exact bound. This is not the randomized MPC implementation and is not claimed to use CONGEST bandwidth.

assumptions: Fixed excluded minor H
Maximize agreements on signed network edges

results.notes: Separate from weighted general graphs and complete-signed minimum-disagreement instances. The proof gathers each component and computes an optimal clustering locally; local computational work is not bounded polynomially. Round exponents are independent of H, while constants may depend on H. Footnote 1 also notes a general-graph LOCAL (1−ε) approximation via low-diameter decomposition; we do not promote that brief observation to an additional fully audited theorem.
